prompt: Colorado Springs has a sunny, dry climate with clear skies most days. Seattle, Washington has a cloudy, rainy climate with many overcast days. Which of the following best explains why solar panels in Colorado Springs can generate more electricity than solar panels in Seattle?
note: Colorado Springs receives ~5.5-5.7 peak sun hours daily versus Seattle's ~3.5 PSH; clear skies account for this difference. IMPORTANT NUANCE: Colorado Springs' elevation (6,000+ feet) also significantly contributes—thinner atmosphere increases solar irradiance by ~10-12% per 1,000 meters of elevation. Quiz answer may be incomplete if it only attributes the difference to cloud cover, ignoring elevation's substantial effect.
source: TurbineGenerator.org, SolarPanel.news, and elevation/irradiance studies confirm both cloud cover and elevation contribute to Colorado Springs' solar advantage.
